target.title: feat(dashboard): sandboxed custom widgets + approval flow [3/3]
target.body:
# Sandboxed custom widgets + approval flow (3/3)

> **The dashboard your agent builds with you.** This is the capability nothing else in the ecosystem has: an agent authors a real HTML widget, it renders live inside the operator's dashboard, and it does so inside a sandbox strict enough that independent security review couldn't break out of it. This is the last mile between "the agent describes a dashboard" and "the agent builds it."

![End-to-end: an agent scaffolds a custom revenue-chart widget, a pending-approval card appears, the operator approves it, the sandboxed iframe mounts and renders live data through the bridge, then the human keeps working the composed grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/dashboard-demo.gif)

*▶ Full-quality recording ([light](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/modular-dashboard-demo-v1/dashboard-demo.mp4) / [dark](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/modular-dashboard-demo-v1/dashboard-demo-dark.mp4)).*

> **Stack note.** This is the top of a three-PR stack (#101094 backend → #101097 UI → #101098 here). The reviewable new work in *this* PR is the sandboxed custom-widget host — ~1,400 lines of source across 9 files, well under VISION.md's ~5K reviewable-line guideline. Because we don't have upstream write access to set GitHub-native stacked bases, all three PRs target `main` with cumulative diffs, so this branch's diff includes #101094's and #101097's commits until they merge to `main` — **review #101094 and #101097 first, then read this PR's `extensions/dashboard/src/{http-route,serve,manifest}.ts` and `ui/src/{components/dashboard-custom-widget,lib/dashboard/bridge}.ts` as the delta.** This same branch is also the full feature end-to-end — check it out to run everything.

## Run the whole thing

Because this PR sits at the top of the stack, checking it out gives you the complete modular-dashboard feature in one branch — no need to assemble the stack yourself:

```sh
gh pr checkout <this-PR-number>       # or: git fetch <fork> feat/modular-dashboard && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
pnpm install && pnpm build
# start the gateway with the dashboard plugin enabled, open the Control UI → the "Workspaces" tab
```

The default **Overview-as-data** workspace renders on first load. Ask an agent (or run `openclaw dashboard tabs create --title Financials`) to build a tab and watch it appear live; scaffold a custom widget, approve it from the pending card, and watch the sandboxed iframe mount. CI runs against this full integration.

## What problem this solves

#101094 and #101097 get an operator most of the way there with a live grid and trusted, built-in widgets — but the actual bet of this whole series is that an agent can build something *bespoke*: a chart, a custom view, a one-off tool, authored on the spot in response to "build me a revenue chart." That means running agent-authored code inside the operator's browser, which is the one place in this series that needs to be provably safe before it ships, not just believed safe.

## What's in this PR

- **Scaffold → pending → approve → mount lifecycle.** An agent (via the `dashboard_widget_scaffold` tool from #101094) creates a widget directory with a manifest and an `index.html`; it enters the registry as `status: "pending"`. A pending widget renders as a placeholder card (name, author, Approve/Reject) — **no iframe is ever created for a pending or rejected widget, on either the client or the server.** Approval routes through the existing plugin-approvals infrastructure as well as an inline Approve button, so it shows up wherever operators already look for approvals.
- **Sandboxed iframe host** (`ui/src/components/dashboard-custom-widget.ts`): `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` — never `allow-same-origin`, never any other token. The sandbox attribute is treated as a constant, not configuration.
- **A versioned, minimal postMessage bridge** (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bridge.ts`): the widget can ask for its declared data bindings and a theme snapshot, and — only with an explicit manifest capability plus a per-invocation operator confirm dialog — ask to send a prompt into chat. The parent only ever accepts messages from the exact iframe window it created, only recognizes a fixed set of message types, and only resolves bindings the widget's own manifest declared — a widget cannot request data it wasn't given permission to see.
- **Static-file-only asset serving**: a new unauthenticated plugin HTTP route (necessary — sandboxed frames carry no device token) that serves *only* files inside the widget's own directory, behind a charset check on the widget name, path normalization, and a containment check, with a locked-down `Content-Security-Policy` (including `connect-src 'none'`, so "no network" is structural, not just a convention) on every response. Only `approved` widgets are served at all — pending/rejected widgets 404 server-side, independent of whatever the client does.
- **Theme sync**: widgets receive the Control UI's current theme tokens so agent-authored UI matches the operator's chosen theme (including #99289's light palette) without the widget author having to guess.

## See it

The full scaffold → pending → approve → mount → live lifecycle, one frame at a time:

**1. Pending — the iframe does not exist yet.** A scaffolded widget lands as a placeholder card (name, author, Approve/Reject). No iframe is constructed on the client, and the assets 404 server-side, until an operator approves.

![A custom widget in the pending-approval card: "Revenue Chart — awaiting approval, built by finance agent," with Approve and Reject affordances and no iframe rendered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/03-financials-pending-approval.png)

**2. Approved and mounted.** After the operator approves, the sandboxed iframe mounts and renders — here an approved custom chart widget on the composed Financials tab, alongside AI-provenance chips and the finance-activity lifecycle feed.

![The composed Financials tab with the approved, sandboxed custom widget rendering a chart, AI-provenance chips, and the Finance Activity lifecycle feed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/04-approved-sandboxed-chart.png)

**3. Live.** A bound value updates in place as the finance agent writes new data — the widget never fetched anything; the parent pushed the resolved binding over the bridge.

![The approved custom widget with a bound revenue value updating live, driven by a data push through the bridge rather than any network call from the widget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/05-live-revenue-update.png)

The same composed Financials tab in the dark theme, kebab menu open, sandboxed widget rendering — agent-authored UI adopts the operator's theme tokens automatically:

![Dark theme: the composed Financials dashboard with the sandboxed custom widget rendering and a widget cell's kebab menu open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/financials-composed-dark.png)

## How it works

The design principle is one sentence: **the widget is untrusted agent-authored code, so it gets no origin, no network, no credentials, and no direct line to the gateway — the trusted parent does everything on its behalf.** Every mechanism below is a consequence of that.

### The key insight: the widget never talks to the gateway

A custom widget is HTML/JS an *agent* wrote. It renders in the operator's browser but is treated as hostile. It has no way to reach the gateway: the sandbox denies it an origin, the CSP denies it the network, and it holds no token. All data reaches it through a single narrow channel — the parent resolves the widget's *declared* bindings and posts the results in. If the widget wants data it wasn't granted, there is no request it can make that succeeds. That inversion (parent-resolves-on-behalf, never widget-fetches) is what makes running agent-authored code in the operator's browser defensible.

### Rendering — a constant `allow-scripts` sandbox

The host component (`ui/src/components/dashboard-custom-widget.ts`) mounts `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" referrerpolicy="no-referrer">`. The sandbox attribute is a **constant string**, not configuration — never `allow-same-origin`, never `allow-top-navigation`, `allow-popups`, or `allow-forms`. With `allow-scripts` alone, the frame's origin is opaque (serializes as `"null"`), so it can never touch the parent's storage, cookies, or DOM. The code comments call this out explicitly ("do not templatize") so a future well-meaning edit can't loosen it.

### Serving — a static-only, path-jailed, approval-gated route

Sandboxed frames carry no device token, so the asset route (`extensions/dashboard/src/http-route.ts`) is registered `auth:"plugin"` (unauthenticated). That is safe *only because* the route is static-file-only and can leak nothing:

- **Name and path**: `/plugins/dashboard/widgets/<name>/<path...>` — `<name>` passes the canvas charset check (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`); `<path...>` is URL-decoded, logically normalized, and containment-checked against the widget's own directory (the `extensions/canvas/src/documents.ts` idiom, reused verbatim).
- **Every rejection is a 404, never a 403** — a traversal attempt, a bad charset, a disallowed extension, or a non-GET method is indistinguishable from a miss, so the route leaks no existence information.
- **Content type is allowlisted by extension** (html/js/css/json/svg/png/jpg/webp/woff2/txt/md/csv); anything else 404s.
- **Strict CSP on every response**: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. `connect-src 'none'` makes "no network" **structural**, not conventional.
- **Approval gate at serve time**: the handler checks the registry and serves *only* widgets whose `status === "approved"`. Pending/rejected widgets 404 server-side, independent of anything the client does — so approval-bypass is enforced where the bytes are, not merely in the UI.

### The bridge — versioned, window-identity-filtered, allowlist-re-checked

Data reaches the widget through a versioned postMessage bridge (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bridge.ts`, envelope `{ v:1, type, … }`), whose security logic is deliberately DOM-free so it's unit-testable in isolation:

- **Accept filter by window identity**: the parent accepts a message only when `event.source === iframe.contentWindow`. Origin strings are useless here (a sandboxed origin is `"null"`), so identity is the check — a message from any other window, including a second widget's iframe, is dropped.
- **Fixed message set, declared bindings only**: the parent recognizes a closed set of types and resolves only bindings the widget's *own manifest* declared, by `bindingId`. `file`/`static` bindings resolve via `dashboard.data.read` (server re-validates the jail); `rpc` bindings are called by the parent on its own gateway client — and the method is **re-checked at resolve time** against the browser-side mirror of the plugin's write-time allowlist (`RPC_METHOD_ALLOWLIST`), a defense-in-depth check on top of PR1's write-time gate. A widget cannot request a binding or method it wasn't granted.
- **Parent→child posts use `targetOrigin "*"`** (required for an opaque child origin) — acceptable *by construction* because the only payloads ever posted are binding data and theme tokens the widget is already entitled to. No config, no session data, no tokenized URLs are ever sent.
- **`sendPrompt` is triple-gated**: it requires the manifest capability `prompt:send`, then a per-invocation operator **confirm dialog** quoting the exact text, then it's **rate-limited** (1 in-flight + 10/min per widget) before it reaches the existing chat-send path.
- **Theme sync**: `getTheme` returns the Control UI's current CSS custom-property tokens (including #99289's light palette) so agent-authored UI matches the operator's theme without the author guessing.

### Approval lifecycle

An agent-scaffolded widget (`dashboard_widget_scaffold`, from #101094) enters `widgetsRegistry` as `status:"pending"`. A pending widget renders the placeholder card — **no iframe is constructed, client or server**. Approval routes through the existing plugin-approvals infrastructure (so it appears wherever operators already look for approvals) as well as the card's inline Approve button → `dashboard.widget.approve` → re-broadcast. Only `approved` widgets ever get an iframe, and only `approved` widgets are ever served — the gate is double-enforced, UI and server.

### Then we tried to break it

This layer got an independent adversarial security review before being proposed here, specifically because it's the highest-security-surface part of the project. The review's job was to try to refute three claims — the path-jail on asset serving, the iframe sandbox, and the CSP — and it could not refute any of them, across two independent passes and dozens of live probes against the running implementation (path traversal variants, encoded/absolute/backslash/symlink-out paths, sandbox-attribute inspection, and a live `connect-src 'none'` network test).

The review did find one real gap: a prompt-dispatch rate limit that didn't survive a widget being removed and re-added (a remount could reset the counter). That was fixed — the rate limiter is now keyed independently of widget lifecycle and covered by a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after — plus a second, defense-in-depth check added at resolve time and a test that keeps the UI-side allowlist mirror in sync with the server-side one. Nothing else from the review was left open.

The resulting safety story, concretely:
- **Rendering** is `allow-scripts` only — no `allow-same-origin`, so the iframe's origin is opaque and it can never touch the parent's storage, cookies, or DOM.
- **Serving** is static-file-only, path-jailed, and gated on registry approval status server-side — approval bypass isn't a client-trust question, it's enforced where the bytes are served from.
- **Networking** is structurally blocked (`connect-src 'none'` in the CSP), not just discouraged by convention.
- **Data** only ever reaches the widget through the bridge, resolved by the authenticated parent against the widget's own declared bindings — the widget itself never holds a credential and never talks to the gateway directly.
- **Prompt dispatch** is capability-gated in the manifest, confirm-dialog-gated per invocation, and rate-limited independent of the widget's mount/unmount lifecycle.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Agents cannot author bespoke widgets that render in the operator's dashboard, because running agent-authored HTML in the browser is unsafe without a hard sandbox. This PR adds the sandboxed custom-widget host: an `allow-scripts`-only iframe (opaque origin), a static-only, path-jailed, approval-gated serving route with `connect-src 'none'`, and a window-identity-filtered postMessage bridge where the trusted parent resolves the widget's declared bindings on its behalf — so an agent-scaffolded widget renders only after operator approval and never talks to the gateway directly.

**Evidence:** 79 plugin + 284 UI tests pass, including the path-jail suite (traversal, encoded traversal, absolute, backslash, symlink-out, name-charset, disallowed extension, non-GET → all 404 with `Content-Security-Policy` + `X-Content-Type-Options` asserted on every response), the bridge suite (foreign-window postMessage dropped, undeclared-binding denial, `sendPrompt` capability-gate + confirm dialog + rate limit), and the custom-widget E2E (approve → mount, a live `fetch()` from the widget blocked by CSP, the sandbox attribute asserted to be exactly `allow-scripts`, and the kill test). An independent adversarial review could not refute the path-jail, sandbox, or CSP across two passes and dozens of live probes; the one hole it found (a prompt rate limit that reset on widget remount) is fixed with a regression test that fails before and passes after. The scaffold → pending → approve → mount → live lifecycle is in the stills above and the recording.

## Verification

**Size:** ~1,400 lines of reviewable source across 9 files (the sandboxed-widget host) — comfortably inside VISION.md's ~5K reviewable-line guideline.

- Path-jail suite: traversal (`../`), encoded traversal, absolute paths, backslash variants, symlink-out, name-charset violations, disallowed extensions, non-GET requests — all 404, with correct `Content-Security-Policy` and `X-Content-Type-Options` headers asserted on every response.
- Bridge suite: handshake, foreign-window postMessage correctly ignored, unknown message types dropped, undeclared binding requests denied, `sendPrompt` without capability denied without even showing a dialog, with capability shows the dialog and sends exactly once on confirm / nothing on deny, rate-limit behavior under remount.
- E2E: `connect-src 'none'` asserted against a live `fetch()` from inside a widget; sandbox attribute asserted to be exactly `allow-scripts` via DOM inspection; the kill test (a throwing widget produces an isolated error card, siblings and other tabs unaffected); the full approve → mount → live-update round trip against a fixture widget.
- The plugin serve/manifest/path-jail suites and the UI bridge + custom-widget suites pass (79 plugin + 284 UI tests), plus the custom-widget E2E (approve → mount, foreign-window drop, CSP `fetch()` block, sandbox-attribute assertion, kill test). CI runs on this PR.

## Closes / part of

Closes **#66983** / **#68497** (agent-rendered UI reachable from the browser — this is exactly that, with the safety work done up front). Partially addresses **#27574** (browser preview panel — the custom-widget host covers the "agent shows me something in the browser" half; a dedicated standalone preview panel outside the dashboard grid is not in scope here). Part of #101093. Builds on #101094, #101097 (top of the stack). With all three merged, the full end-to-end flow in the recording above — agent composes a tab, scaffolds and approves a sandboxed widget, live updates, human reorders — is reproducible against a running gateway.

target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

## Evidence

Current head: `8bbd81367e8807a741314b9a91cfb99d24b4586e`.
Current base: `6db0506474ceb10c64ea3b5f64e29772fb04280e`.

### Current-head runtime proof

Isolated config with `main` present and `ops` marked as `agents.list[].default` validates cleanly, and `agents list --json` reports `ops` as the default without promoting `main`:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "main",
    "isDefault": false,
    "agentDir": "<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent",
    "workspace": "<home>/.openclaw/workspace-main"
  },
  {
    "id": "ops",
    "isDefault": true,
    "agentDir": "<home>/.openclaw/agents/ops/agent",
    "workspace": "<home>/.openclaw/workspace"
  }
]
```

Direct runtime proof with configured agents `utility` and default `ops`, plus an existing on-disk `agents/main/agent` store, shows the new default surfaces consistently use `ops` while still discovering the old `main` store:

```json
{
  "defaultAgentId": "ops",
  "defaultAgentDir": "<state>/agents/ops/agent",
  "sessionKey": "agent:ops:main",
  "sessionStorePath": "<state>/agents/ops/sessions/sessions.json",
  "transcriptDir": "<state>/agents/ops/sessions",
  "authStoreAgentDirs": [
    "<state>/agents/ops/agent",
    "<state>/agents/main/agent",
    "<state>/agents/utility/agent"
  ],
  "modelsJsonPaths": [
    "<state>/agents/ops/agent/models.json",
    "<state>/agents/main/agent/models.json",
    "<state>/agents/utility/agent/models.json"
  ],
  "auditFinding": {
    "checkId": "agents.claude_cli.permission_mode_overridden_by_yolo",
    "severity": "warn",
    "detail": "claude-cli sets args=default, but OpenClaw exec is YOLO for: ops, utility, ops. Managed Claude live sessions use --permission-mode bypassPermissions."
  }
}
```

That covers the requested proof surfaces: session key/store path, setup transcript path, auth/model scan discovery, audit output, and explicit preservation/discovery of an existing `agents/main` store without treating `main` as the configured default.

### Local validation

- Focused default-agent tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/storage-scan.default-agent.test.ts src/agents/command/session.resolve-session-key.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.test.ts src/config/sessions/paths.default-agent.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-surface.test.ts` — passed 4 Vitest shards / 41 tests on current head.
- Core typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` — passed on current head.
- Formatting: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` over the 14 touched files — passed on current head.
- Touched-file lint: `pnpm exec oxlint` over the 14 touched files — passed on current head.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed on current head.
- Pre-PR preview: `~/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/openclaw-pre-pr.sh --repo /root/projects/openclaw-pr-51762 --plan-only` completed after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`.

GitHub checks are expected to re-run for this pushed head.

Closes #90573.
Supersedes stale #17477 without adding the previously proposed config/env fallback surface.

target.title: feat(android): add Skill Workshop settings panel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Settings did not expose the Skill Workshop review queue, so mobile users could not inspect generated skill proposals or perform the same core proposal lifecycle actions available from the Web UI. This left proposal review dependent on desktop/Web access even when the Android app was already connected to a Gateway.

## Summary

- Add a dedicated Android Settings > Skill Workshop panel for proposal review.
- Load proposal lists and details through existing Gateway `skills.proposals.*` RPCs with agent-scope support.
- Auto-load selected proposal details to match Web controller behavior.
- Support pending proposal lifecycle actions from mobile: apply, reject, and quarantine.
- Add Settings home summary counts and filtering/search helper coverage.

## Implementation Notes

- The Android UI uses a mobile list/detail layout rather than the Web desktop board layout.
- No new Gateway API is introduced; Android reuses the existing Skill Workshop RPC methods.
- Gateway responses are guarded against stale list/detail updates during gateway changes.

## Evidence

- Local static checks passed on the PR branch:
  - `git diff --check`
  - `git diff --cached --check`
- Added unit coverage for Skill Workshop settings summary and filtering helpers in `ShellScreenLogicTest`.
- GitHub Actions on this PR has reported passing checks for Workflow Sanity `no-tabs`, `actionlint`, OpenGrep PR diff, dependency guard, security-sensitive guard, Socket PR alerts, CI `runner-admission`, `preflight`, and `security-fast`.
- Android-specific CI checks are running on GitHub Actions for this branch, including `android-ktlint`, `android-build-play`, `android-test-play`, and `android-test-third-party`.

## Not Run Locally

- Android ktlint/build/tests were not run locally because this environment has no `java`/`JAVA_HOME` available. The Android verification matrix is running in GitHub Actions.

## Risk

- Moderate UI/RPC surface change isolated to Android Settings and existing Skill Workshop Gateway methods.
- No dependency, workflow, release, or Gateway API surface changes.

target.title: Dashboard: stream + computed data-binding kinds
target.body:
> Live push feeds and derived values, not just files: bind a widget to a gateway event stream, or compute one from other bindings — safely, with no new network and no expression language.

Closes #101150. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `schema.ts` / `index.ts` / `data-read.ts` deltas.

## What's in this PR
Two new binding kinds alongside the existing `file` / `static` / `rpc`:
- **`stream`** — push updates from an **allowlisted** gateway broadcast channel. It does **not** open a socket: it multiplexes over the Control UI's existing gateway WebSocket via `client.addEventListener`, and the event id must be one of a small `STREAM_EVENT_ALLOWLIST` (`presence`, `sessions.changed`, `plugin.dashboard.changed` — all read-only). Enforced at write time in the schema *and* re-checked at subscribe time (defense-in-depth), so a stream binding can never listen on an arbitrary channel. Unsubscribes on unmount.
- **`computed`** — a value derived from the resolved values of *sibling* bindings via exactly one **fixed, whitelisted op**: `sum · avg · min · max · count · last · pick(pointer) · format(template)`. It's a `switch` — **no expression language, no `eval`, no `Function`**. `pick` is a read-only pointer traversal; `format` interpolates resolved values into a bounded template.

**Deliberately excluded:** a `command:` binding (running shell commands) is *not* here — arbitrary command execution deserves its own security-reviewed PR, so it's carved out.

## How it works & why it's safe
`resolveBinding` gains branches on both sides (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/index.ts` client, `extensions/dashboard/src/data-read.ts` server returns a typed client-resolved marker like `rpc` does), and the schema union validates both kinds strictly. Two structural safety properties:
- **No arbitrary network** — `stream` is an allowlist over already-published gateway events on the existing socket; there is no code path to an external URL.
- **No cycles, no code exec** — a `computed` input may only reference a *non-computed* binding, which makes a reference cycle structurally impossible (no graph walk needed); and the op set is a closed switch, so there's no evaluator to exploit.

No new dependency.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bindings were limited to `file` / `static` / `rpc` — no way to push-update a widget from a live event or derive a value from other bindings without polling. This adds `stream` (allowlisted gateway events, multiplexed over the existing socket) and `computed` (fixed op set), with `command:` deliberately deferred to its own reviewed PR.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard` green — schema accept/reject for both kinds (unknown op, malformed inputs, non-allowlisted event, computed→computed rejection), each computed op's result, and stream subscribe→push→unsubscribe over a mocked event source; `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run.

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

Validated on the rebased head `b92cbeb709e62ecf4d8e821067e4cfa20314ffbb`, based on current `origin/main` `6db05064`:

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatTranscriptCacheStoreTests` (39 tests passed)
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter ChatTranscriptCache` (6 tests passed)

target.title: fix(installer): complete first-run onboarding
target.body:
## Summary

- send fresh installs into onboarding before doctor or gateway finalization probes
- use the just-installed OpenClaw binary for follow-up commands and explain `hash -r` when the shell still caches a removed path
- let onboarding persist gateway configuration and authentication before installing or starting the managed service
- preserve doctor, plugin update, gateway restart, and dashboard behavior for configured upgrades
- add installer regression coverage for fresh installs, upgrades, no-TTY behavior, stale PATH resolution, and gateway finalization

## What Problem This Solves

A fresh git install could report success without creating `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, gateway authentication, or a managed gateway service. Its suggested follow-up then failed first through a stale `/usr/bin/openclaw` shell lookup, and subsequently through missing gateway mode/auth/service state. The TUI also failed with `Missing gateway auth token` because setup had never completed.

This change makes first-run onboarding the installer finalization path. Doctor and gateway health behavior remain on the configured-upgrade path instead of being used as a substitute for initial setup.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`

- earlier exact-patch proof: formatting, ShellCheck, focused tests, onboarding/Crestodian Docker scenarios, gateway-auth tests, and the changed-files gate passed
- rebased patch ID matches the reviewed and tested pre-rebase patch

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Fresh `--install-method git --version main` installs could finish without first-run config, gateway auth, or a managed gateway service, then recommend commands that could not work in that state.

Real environment tested: Linux installer regression coverage plus onboarding/Crestodian Docker scenarios and gateway-auth scenarios on the same patch.

target.body:
## Summary

- extend marketplace feed verification config to support signed mode with local Ed25519 signing keys and an optional threshold
- validate signed feed trust anchors in the OpenClaw config schema, including key shape, strict raw base64url public-key parsing, private-key rejection, unique key IDs, unique normalized public keys, and threshold bounds
- document the new config fields in generated help and labels, and carry the verification shape into the official external catalog feed profile type
- fail closed for signed feed profiles until refresh envelope enforcement is wired, without fetching, reading snapshots, or returning bundled public entries for that selected profile

## Stack

- Stacked after #98299 (`feeds-trust-envelope-verifier`).
- This PR intentionally targets `main` as a draft because the dependency branch is on the fork; review should focus on the top commit `16cbe678ce` until #98299 lands.

## Scope boundaries

This is still a config-contract slice. It does not verify signed feed envelopes during marketplace refresh yet, does not persist snapshot trust state, does not add CLI/operator trust output, and does not change install eligibility. Signed profiles are accepted as local trust config but return zero marketplace entries until the later enforcement slice consumes signed envelopes.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxlint --deny-warnings src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`

- `codex review --base fork/feeds-trust-envelope-verifier` - clean after ClawSweeper/Codex hardening fixes

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
OpenClaw config now accepts signed marketplace feed verification profiles only when local Ed25519 public signing keys are provided and the optional threshold is valid. Invalid signed profiles fail schema parsing, including malformed raw base64url keys, duplicate key IDs, and duplicate normalized public keys. If a signed profile is selected before refresh envelope enforcement is wired, the hosted catalog loader fails closed by returning no entries and does not fetch the feed, read unsigned snapshots, or return bundled public catalog entries for that selected profile.

Real environment tested:
Windows source checkout at `C:\src\openclaw-feeds-trust-source-profiles`, stacked on #98299 head `8742cc6515`; source-level config schema tests, hosted catalog loader tests, targeted OpenClaw validation commands, and Codex review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Evidence after fix:
The focused marketplace schema, generated-help quality, and hosted catalog loader tests passed with 23, 12, and 52 tests respectively. Targeted lint, targeted format, whitespace checks, and Codex review completed without findings.

Observed result after fix:
Signed marketplace feed config with valid local Ed25519 public keys and threshold parses successfully; missing keys, empty keys, invalid public keys, malformed raw base64url public keys, private PEM values, duplicate key IDs, duplicate normalized public keys, zero threshold, and threshold greater than key count are rejected. Selecting a signed feed profile before enforcement is wired returns a non-throwing fallback result with zero entries and does not call the fetch path.

What was not tested:
Live marketplace refresh of a signed envelope was not tested because this PR intentionally does not wire signed envelope enforcement into refresh or snapshot persistence yet.

target.title: Dashboard: ops widgets — agent status + approvals queue
target.body:
> The operational half of the builtin set: see what every agent is doing, and act on what's waiting for you — from a dashboard cell.

Closes #101145 and #101144. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `agent-status.ts` + `approvals.ts` and their wiring as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**`builtin:agent-status` (#101145)** — a compact per-agent/session status list: active-run vs idle, current label, and freshness — the "what's everything doing right now?" glance. It binds to the same `sessions.list` data the `sessions` builtin already uses (no new backend), so it live-updates on the existing broadcast path.

**`builtin:approvals` (#101144)** — a pending-approvals queue with Approve/Deny actions, wired end-to-end through the **existing** widget-approval infrastructure from #101098 (`dashboard.widget.approve`): pending `custom:` widgets appear as cards, and a decision dispatches the same client path the Workspaces pending-card uses. The queue arrives via a new `ctx.approvals` source on the builtin context (mirroring the existing `ctx.embed` pattern), because it's in-memory workspace state rather than an RPC binding.

**Scope note (deliberate):** the gateway's exec/plugin approval RPCs (`exec.approval.*`, `plugin.approval.*`) exist and the app shell uses them, but they are operator-scoped and not in the dashboard's read-only binding allowlist (`DATA_READ_RPC_ALLOWLIST`). Widening that allowlist is a security decision we didn't want to smuggle into a widget PR — so this widget covers the dashboard's own approval queue today, and is shaped to take exec/plugin approvals as additional sources the moment maintainers bless that allowlist addition (called out in the module header). That keeps #72545 progressing without expanding any privilege surface.

## How it works
Both widgets follow the established builtin contract (`renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult`), registered in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` + `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN`. Agent-status is a pure mapper over the resolved `sessions.list` value. Approvals renders from `ctx.approvals` (built by the dashboard view from workspace state) and dispatches decisions through the existing, already-authorized `dashboard.widget.approve` method — this PR adds **no new gateway method and no new privilege**.

No new dependency — `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** There's no cross-agent activity view in the dashboard (#101145 / the #39127–#54577 cluster), and approvals had no dashboard surface (#101144, advancing #72545) — operators had to open each session or wait for the pending-card to appear on the Workspaces tab. This adds two operational builtins: a live agent-status list and an approvals queue with working Approve/Deny.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 100 passed, including the new suites (status derivation filters + provenance, decision-vocabulary mapping + limit, populated/empty renders, and Approve/Deny wiring asserted against a mocked client dispatching `dashboard.widget.approve`); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and full type-aware oxlint clean; `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` green (schema kind additions).

target.title: Dashboard: inter-widget pub/sub — a tab-scoped, parent-brokered message bus
target.body:
> Widgets on the same tab can finally talk to each other — a filter widget drives a chart, a selector narrows a table — without ever being able to reach a widget on another tab.

Closes #101147. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `bus.ts` + the `bridge.ts` / host changes as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- Bridge messages `dashboard:publish` / `dashboard:subscribe` / `dashboard:unsubscribe` (inbound) delivering as `dashboard:message` (outbound), gated behind a new `bus:pubsub` manifest capability.
- A parent-brokered, DOM-free bus (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bus.ts`): widgets never talk directly — the trusted parent fans a published payload out to the *other* same-tab subscribers on that channel.
- Caps: 8 KB payload, 60 publishes / 60 s (keyed by stable widget name so a remount can't reset the budget), 256-char channel names.

## Security model (this is the point of the design)
- **Tab isolation is structural, not a filter.** The subscription table is keyed `tabSlug → channel → subscriberId`, and a publish only ever iterates the *publisher's own tab bucket*. A widget on tab A cannot observe — or even enumerate — a subscriber on tab B; cross-tab delivery is unreachable code, not a rejected case.
- **Identity is broker-assigned.** The host mints an opaque `subscriberId` the widget never sees, and binds `tabSlug` from the widget's real tab (`tab.slug` in `renderGrid`) — both are closed over in the parent; a child message only ever carries an opaque `channel` + `payload`. A widget can't spoof another's identity, target a specific peer, or name a tab it wasn't assigned to. The publisher is excluded from its own broadcast.
- **No new reach.** The bus is in-memory and parent-brokered only — it never touches the gateway and never persists. The capability gate, size cap, and rate limit sit alongside the existing `sendPrompt` gates in `bridge.ts`; the `event.source` window-identity filter still guards the new inbound types; opaque origin unchanged.

All of the above is covered by tests (same-tab delivery, cross-tab non-delivery, publisher exclusion, capability denial both directions, size/rate caps, unmount teardown, unexpected-window rejection). No new dependency.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Dashboard widgets were fully isolated, so they couldn't compose — a filter widget had no way to drive a chart on the same tab. This adds a parent-brokered, tab-scoped pub/sub bus, capability-gated and rate/size-capped, with cross-tab isolation guaranteed by construction.
**Evidence:** `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/components` green including the bus/bridge/host suites (tab-isolation, publisher-exclusion, capability gate, caps, unmount sweep); `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, and full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run (not agent-reported).

target.title: Dashboard: workspace time-travel + blame
target.body:
# Dashboard: workspace time-travel + blame

> Scrub your dashboard through its own history, diff any snapshot against now (grouped by who changed what), and click a widget to jump to the agent session that created it.

Closes #101822. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the history RPCs, `history.ts`, and the panel/blame UI as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **Read-only history RPCs** — `dashboard.workspace.history.list` / `.get` (both `operator.read`) over the existing 20-entry undo ring. `list` returns `{ version, savedAt, bytes }` newest-first (metadata only, never bodies); `get(version)` returns one snapshot.
- **History panel** — a toolbar button opens a modal: the version list, a read-only preview render of any snapshot, a **diff vs current** grouped by actor (tab/widget added / removed / moved / retitled), and **restore** (wired to the existing single-step `dashboard.workspace.undo`, offered only on the newest snapshot).
- **Blame** — the cell menu shows "created by `agent:main` · vN"; for agent authors it links to the logbook (#99930) when that tab is advertised, so the dashboard becomes auditable and the logbook gains a spatial index.

## How it works
Everything is a **read-only** surface over state that already existed: the undo ring (snapshots), `workspaceVersion`, and `createdBy` provenance. The ring-read API parses ring files without mutating them; restore reuses the existing undo write (no new write RPC); the diff indexes widgets by id and tabs by slug across two docs. No new dependency, no new write privilege.

**Honest limitations (called out in-code):** restore is single-step (the ring is an undo ring, so only the most recent change is revertible); the logbook is a day-keyed snapshot journal with no URL-addressable session/day, so blame links to the logbook tab root rather than a specific entry; first-seen version resolves only once snapshot bodies are loaded (the panel), falling back to provenance-only.

## Real behavior proof

target.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — persist widget state via a setState bridge capability
target.body:
> Give sandboxed widgets memory: a jailed, approval-gated `setState` capability that turns custom widgets from views into stateful apps.

Closes #101137. **Stacked on #101098** (the sandboxed custom-widget host) — that PR lands first; this targets `main` with a cumulative diff, so review the new `state`-related files as the delta.

## What problem this solves
Custom widgets today are read-only: the postMessage bridge lets a widget *ask* the parent for data, but there's no way to *save* anything — so an agent-built notes pad, kanban, or game resets on every reload. This adds the one missing primitive: per-widget, jailed, size-capped state, without loosening the sandbox.

## What's in this PR
- New gateway RPCs `dashboard.widget.state.get` / `.set` (read/write scoped), persisting to a path-jailed, size-capped per-widget file under `<stateDir>/dashboard/state/<widgetId>.json` — atomic writes, kept *separate* from `workspace.json` (does not count against the 256 KB workspace cap).
- New bridge inbound messages `dashboard:setState` / `getState`, gated behind a new `state:persist` manifest capability (mirrors the existing `sendPrompt` gate).
- The trusted parent resolves the widget's own `widgetId` — a widget can never read or write another widget's state, and a widget-supplied id is ignored.
- Unit tests covering the store round-trip (persist → read-back), the 64 KB size-cap whole-reject, widget-id charset/traversal rejects, the capability gate, read/write scope, and state-vs-workspace separation — the `extensions/dashboard` suite (85 tests) and the UI dashboard suite (94 tests) are green.
- This PR is the capability + its plumbing; the first shippable consumer is the stateful notes/todo widget (#101146), which depends on it.

## How it works
The design mirrors the read path from #101098: **the widget never holds a credential and never talks to the gateway** — the trusted Control-UI parent brokers everything. On `dashboard:setState`, the parent calls `dashboard.widget.state.set` with the `widgetId` *it* already tracks for that iframe (`widget.id`); the widget's message carries only the opaque blob, and the `setWidgetState` bridge dependency takes *only* the blob — there is no code path by which a widget names another widget's state. State is capped at **64 KB** per widget (the serialized envelope, rejected whole *before* any write), stored under `<stateDir>/dashboard/state/<widgetId>.json` (`0o700` dir / `0o600` file), serialized through the store's process mutex and written atomically via `replaceFileAtomic`. The widget id is charset-guarded (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$`) and the resolved path is re-checked for containment. The new `plugin.dashboard.widget-state.changed` broadcast carries `{ widgetId, version }` only — never the blob.

## Security
This widens the trust surface, so it carries the same adversarial-review discipline as #101098. Verified in code and tests:
- **(a) Own-state only** — the `widgetId` is always `widget.id`, bound by the trusted parent; the `setWidgetState` bridge dependency takes only the blob, and any id in the child's message is ignored.
- **(b) Size cap** — 64 KB enforced on the serialized envelope *before* any write; oversize is rejected whole (nothing written).
- **(c) Path jail** — the id is charset-guarded (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$`) and the resolved `state/<widgetId>.json` path is re-checked for containment.
- **(d) Capability gate** — `state:persist` is required; an ungated widget is denied *without touching the gateway*, the same shape as `sendPrompt`.
- **(e) No new iframe reach** — the iframe still cannot reach the gateway; the parent holds the socket and calls the new RPCs on the widget's behalf.
- **(f) Sandbox unchanged** — opaque origin, CSP `connect-src 'none'`, and the window-identity accept filter are all untouched.

Note: this PR adds **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged, so the dependency-graph guard should not trip.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Sandboxed custom widgets cannot persist their own state (the bridge is read-only), so any agent- or user-built interactive widget resets on reload. This adds a jailed, size-capped, capability-gated `setState`/`getState` path so a widget can save and restore its own state.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 85 passed (store persist/read-back round-trip, 64 KB whole-reject, widget-id charset/traversal rejects, capability gate, read/write scope, and proof that widget state is written under `state/<widgetId>.json` and never into `workspace.json`); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 94 passed (bridge routes `setState`/`getState` only when the `state:persist` capability is present, and ignores any widget-supplied id); `pnpm ui:build` and oxlint clean.

target.title: Dashboard: chart widgets + widget authoring SDK
target.body:
> Two things that make the widget system easier to *use* and easier to *extend*: a family of dependency-free chart widgets, and a guide + starter templates for authoring your own.

Closes #101142 and #101141. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the new `chart.ts` + `docs/`/`examples/` files as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**Chart widgets (#101142)** — a `builtin:chart` renderer covering five visual types via `props.type`: `line`, `bar`, `area`, `sparkline`, `gauge`.
- Rendered as **dependency-free inline SVG** (lit's `svg` template — no charting library, no new npm dependency).
- Binds to a timeseries `value` through the same binding path every builtin uses; the value shape is tolerant (`number[]`, `{x?, y|value}[]`, or `{points:[…]}`) and normalized to a finite `number[]` before drawing.
- Compact, axis-light visuals that scale to the grid cell; empty/missing data falls back to the shared placeholder; `role="img"` + `aria-label`.

**Widget authoring SDK (#101141)** — `docs/plugins/dashboard-widget-authoring.md` plus three copy-paste starter widgets under `extensions/dashboard/examples/widgets/`.
- The guide documents **both** widget paths: builtin renderers (the `renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult` contract, and registering a kind in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` *and* `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN` — which must change together), and sandboxed custom widgets (the `widget.json` manifest, the postMessage bridge, the approval flow, and the CSP/opaque-origin constraints).
- Starter templates: `hello-data` (reads a binding), `notes` (persists via `getState`/`setState`), and `calculator` (self-contained).

## How it works
The chart widget is a pure renderer: it normalizes the resolved binding value to a numeric series, computes a fixed `100×40` viewBox with padded scaling (flat-lining a zero-range series), and emits `polyline` / `polygon` / `rect` / arc `path` elements per type — the gauge is a 180° arc with a needle at the value's position in `[min,max]`. Nothing fetches; the renderer only draws what its binding resolved. The SDK is documentation + example assets only — no runtime code changes.

Note: the SDK guide's `state:persist` capability and `getState`/`setState` bridge messages (used by the `notes` template) are delivered by the write-back PR (#101137 / #101329); the guide documents them as part of the widget system.

This PR adds **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard had only stat-card and table builtins (no way to visualize a trend), and no documented path for contributors or agents to author new widgets. This adds a dependency-free chart widget family and an authoring guide + starter templates for both the builtin and sandboxed-custom widget paths.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → the UI dashboard suite is green (incl. the chart mapping/render suite: normalize shapes, per-type element counts for line/bar/area/gauge, and empty-state); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and oxlint clean. The chart renders only inside a live dashboard grid with a resolved binding, so it's verified via the render tests per repo idiom.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop
target.body:
# Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop

> Two halves of the flagship interaction: the agent answers show-don't-tell questions by composing a live widget, and widgets can act — a button or form that dispatches a parameterized prompt back to the agent.

Closes #101820 and #101821. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `action-form`, `ephemeral`, and Living-Answers pieces as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **`ephemeral` + pin (#101820)** — a widget may carry `ephemeral: { expiresAt }`; the store sweeps expired ephemeral widgets on read (one atomic write, only when something expired, version bumped), and a **Pin** action in the cell menu clears the marker to make it permanent. So an agent can answer with a self-cleaning widget on an "Answers" tab; a useful answer is one click from permanent.
- **`builtin:action-form` (#101821)** — an operator-authored button/form whose fields interpolate into a `template` and submit dispatches it back to the agent. "Deploy {env}", "Triage {id} as {priority}" become one-click playbooks.
- **Living-Answers convention** — an agent-facing doc (`extensions/dashboard/docs/LIVING-ANSWERS.md`) + 3 worked examples: answer visual questions with a live widget, not prose.

## Security (action-form)
- **No new dispatch privilege.** Submit routes through `dispatchRateLimitedPrompt` — the *exact same* operator-confirm + rate-limit gate the sandboxed custom-widget bridge's `sendPrompt` uses. A test proves an action-form and a same-keyed bridge share one exhausted rate budget.
- **No template injection.** Interpolation is a single pass over the *authored template* with a function replacer: each `{slot}` resolves to its declared field's typed, length-capped value (default 200/field), and the inserted text is never re-scanned — an injected `{evil}` inside a field value stays literal (tested). The template is authored into the workspace document (operator-approvable, schema-validated: ≤2000 chars, ≤8 fields, every `{slot}` must name a declared field).

## How it works
The `ephemeral` marker is a tiny schema addition swept in the store's existing read path; `action-form` is a trusted builtin registered like the others; the dispatch gate was extracted (`dispatchRateLimitedPrompt`) so the builtin and the sandbox bridge share one code path. No new dependency; no new gateway privilege.

Note: this builds on the corrected base (#101098) where the UI↔gateway widget-mutation and file-binding contracts were fixed — pin uses the corrected `{ tab, id, patch }` mutation contract.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard could show data but not *act*, and agent answers to visual questions were prose that died in the transcript. This adds the acting half (an action-form widget that dispatches through the existing gate) and the answering convention (ephemeral answer-widgets + pin).
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` green — schema validation (template/field caps, unknown-slot reject, ISO ephemeral), the store TTL sweep, the single-pass no-double-expansion interpolation, and the shared-rate-budget dispatch; `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full oxlint clean. Counts verified by the submitting orchestrator's own gate: `extensions/dashboard` 94, UI dashboard + plugin-page + cell suites 140.

target.body:
## PR #94697 — Risk Closure Supplement > **Status: ClawSweeper P1/P2 items addressed** ### What changed since v1 (post ClawSweeper review) | Version | Change | Closes | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | | v1 (commit 9fd6116) | Initial leader-check + `detached:true` override | #76259 main case | | v2 (commit 3b261a9) | Propagate `detached:true` through 6 caller sites | ClawSweeper P1 — detached descendant cleanup | | v3 (commit cede936) | Propagate `detached:true` to agent-core NodeExecutionEnv | ClawSweeper P1 — full caller audit | | v4 (commit 7fb01ea) | (a) 4 new fail-safe tests for ps failure modes
(b) `/proc//stat` Linux fallback
(c) Source-level caller audit table | ClawSweeper P1 availability + P2 validation | --- ### ClawSweeper items — closed #### [P1] Compatibility — shared omitted-option Unix cleanup now depends on ps **Status: closed by /proc fallback + fail-safe tests.** The shared `killProcessTree(pid)` path (omitted `detached`) calls `isProcessGroupLeader(pid)`, which now has two layers: 1. **Primary**: `ps -p -o pgid=` (works on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD) 2. **Secondary** (Linux only): `/proc//stat` field 5 (pgid) — works on distroless / scratch / minimal Alpine where `ps` is absent 3. **Tertiary fail-safe**: both fail → returns `false` → single-pid kill (no group kill, no gateway SIGTERM) The fail-safe path is now covered by 4 new tests in `kill-tree.test.ts`: - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps throws - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps exits non-zero - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is non-numeric - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is empty Worst-case behavior on a Linux image without `ps` and without `/proc` (extremely rare — e.g. chroot without procfs): single-pid kill is used. This is **strictly safer than the pre-PR main**, which would have done `process.kill(-pid, ...)` unconditionally and SIGTERM'd the gateway. #### [P1] Availability — detached descendant cleanup after leader exit **Status: closed by v2 caller audit.** The P1 scenario (detached leader exits → `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false → descendants orphaned) is closed by **all 6 detached-spawn callers now explicitly passing `detached: true`** to `killProcessTree` / `signalProcessTree`. The `detached: true` short-circuits the leader check (`opts?.detached === true || ...`), preserving group kill unconditionally. #### Caller audit table (source-level proof) | Caller file | Spawn line | Spawn `detached` value | Cleanup call site | Passes `detached: true`? | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (NodeExecutionEnv.exec) | L319, L321 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L298 (abort), L339 (timeout) | ✅ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (runCommand helper) | L152 | **not set** (attached) | L162 | ✅ correctly **omitted** | | `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L130, L134 | ✅ | | `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` | L83, L87 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L246 | ✅ | | `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` | L445, L447 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L460, L464 | ✅ | | `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L77, L87 | ✅ | | `src/process/exec.ts` (runCommandWithTimeout) | L396, L402 | `killProcessTree && process.platform !== "win32"` (conditional) | L501 (inside `if (killProcessTree)` guard) | ✅ | **Invariant**: every caller that spawns with `detached: true` passes `detached: true` to cleanup; every caller that spawns attached passes nothing (or `detached: false`). The two cannot drift because they share the same `killProcessTree` option flag at the spawn site. #### [P2] Persistent data-model change detected in `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` **Status: false positive — no serialized state change.** The only change to `bash.ts` is on L77 and L87, where the existing `killProcessTree(child.pid)` call gains a second argument `{ detached: true }`. This is a function-call argument change, not a structural change to any persisted type. No `SessionState`, `BashSnapshot`, or serialized payload is touched. The `KillProcessTreeOptions` type itself was already extended with `detached?: boolean` in PR #71681; this PR only consumes the existing field. #### [P2] Run current-head process cleanup validation before merge **Status: closed by validation script.** Ran the exact [P1] acceptance criteria commands from ClawSweeper's review: ```bash # 1. kill-tree unit tests node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/kill-tree.test.ts # 2. agent cleanup paths node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts \ src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts # 3. exec / shell / bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts \ src/process/exec.test.ts ``` Real process-group behavior verified on macOS arm64 (Sequoia): - **Step A**: attached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? false` → single-pid kill used (expected) - **Step B**: detached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? true` → group kill reaches descendants (expected) --- ### Merge readiness - ✅ All ClawSweeper P1 items closed with source-level evidence - ✅ All ClawSweeper P2 items closed (false positive explained + validation run) - ✅ Test count: 19/19 (15 original + 4 fail-safe = 19) - ✅ No API change to `KillProcessTreeOptions` (existing `detached?: boolean` field) - ✅ No new runtime dependency (only `node:fs` for /proc fallback) - ✅ Backwards compatible: pre-PR main callers that omit `detached` see safer behavior (no gateway SIGTERM risk); callers that spawn detached and pass `detached: true` see identical behavior to pre-#71681 main - ✅ Windows path untouched --- **Ready for maintainer review.** --- ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? - `killProcessTree` on Unix defaults `useGroupKill` to `true` when callers omit `{ detached: false }`. If the PID is not its own process group leader, `process.kill(-pid, ...)` targets whatever process group `pid` belongs to — typically the gateway's own process group, causing the gateway to receive SIGTERM. Why does this matter now? - #71681 made the fix opt-in (callers must pass `{ detached: false }`), but any caller that omits the option still triggers the bug. On macOS with launchd-managed gateway, a non-detached child that becomes a zombie triggers `killProcessTree` → `process.kill(-pid, SIGTERM)` → gateway receives SIGTERM and exits. What is the intended outcome? - `killProcessTree` verifies whether the PID is its own process group leader via `ps -p -o pgid=` before using group kill. Non-leader PIDs fall back to single-pid kill, preventing accidental gateway signaling. - When the caller explicitly passes `detached: true`, group kill is used unconditionally (bypassing the leader check), preserving the ability to clean up detached process groups even after the group leader has exited. What is intentionally out of scope? - Windows behavior is unchanged (taskkill /T already handles tree termination correctly). The `detached: false` option is preserved as an explicit caller override. What does success look like? - All 15 vitest tests pass (10 original + 3 original new + 2 new for detached:true override). A non-group-leader PID receives single-pid kill while a group leader PID still receives group kill. A detached:true call forces group kill even after leader exit. What should reviewers focus on? - Whether `isProcessGroupLeader` using `spawnSync("ps", ...)` is acceptable for the kill path (it's not a hot path), and whether the 500ms timeout is appropriate. - The `detached:true` override added for the P1 fix in #94697 review. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes #76259 Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? - Related #71662 (original issue) - Related #71681 (original opt-in fix) - ClawSweeper review #94697 (P1: preserve detached group cleanup after leader exit) Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Reporter issue with numbered repro and suggested fix; ClawSweeper queueable-fix criteria in comments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) **Behavior or issue addressed:** `killProcessTree` group-kill defaults to `true` and can SIGTERM the gateway when the PID is not a process group leader. After leader exit, `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false, but `detached:true` forces group kill. **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64 (Sequoia), local checkout, branch `fix/76259-kill-tree-group-leader` **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash # Run validation script node scripts/validate-94697.mjs # Test process group behavior manually: # 1. Spawn attached child - shares parent's PG (non-leader) node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}); console.log('attached PID',c.pid);" # 2. Spawn detached child - becomes own group leader node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe'],detached:true}); c.unref(); console.log('detached PID',c.pid);" ``` **Evidence after fix:** ``` ============================================================ 1. Unit tests (kill-tree) — platform=darwin ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 2. Agent cleanup paths ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 3. Exec/shell/bash ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 4. Real process-group behavior proof (platform=darwin) ============================================================ ── Step A: attached child shares parent's PG (non-leader) ── child PID=11673 isProcessGroupLeader? false (expected: false on attached child) ── Step B: detached child becomes its own group leader ── child PID=11685 isProcessGroupLeader? true (expected: true) group kill via process.kill(-pid) issued ============================================================ SUMMARY ============================================================ Unit tests (kill-tree): PASS Unit tests (agent cleanup): PASS Unit tests (exec/shell/bash): PASS Overall: ✅ ALL GREEN ``` **Observed result after fix:** - attached child (non-leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `false` → single-pid kill used ✅ - detached child (leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `true` → group kill reaches descendants ✅ - All 19 unit tests pass ✅

target.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a cron job fires `sessionTarget: "main"` with `payload.kind: "systemEvent"` and default `wakeMode: "now"`, if the main-session heartbeat returns a non-retryable skip (e.g. `"disabled"`), the already-enqueued system event was removed and the job returned `status: "skipped"`. The event was silently lost — never delivered to the user.

**Solution**: Two-layer fix — (1) Timer layer: keep system event queued and request deferred heartbeat; (2) Heartbeat layer: bypass per-agent heartbeat config gates for cron-sourced wakes.

**What changed**:

- `src/cron/service/timer.ts`: In `executeMainSessionCronJob()`, the two branches that called `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle()` on heartbeat skip/error are replaced with a single branch that keeps the event queued, schedules a background heartbeat, and returns the original heartbeat status. Returning `"ok"` would cause one-shot jobs with `deleteAfterRun=true` to be immediately deleted, bypassing the bounded disabled-heartbeat retry mechanism.

- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`:
  - `runHeartbeatOnce()`: Wraps the `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` checks in `if (opts.source !== "cron")` — only non-cron sources are gated by per-agent config.
  - Scheduler `run()`: When a cron-targeted wake targets an agent not present in the heartbeat scheduler's agent list, calls `runOnce()` directly instead of returning `{status: "skipped", reason: "disabled"}`.

**What did NOT change**: The heartbeat-`"ran"` path (the common happy path) is untouched. No new dependencies, no config changes, no API surface changes.

Fixes #101537

---

## What Problem This Solves

System events like reminders, scheduled messages, and periodic notifications were silently lost when the main session heartbeat was disabled — a common state when the user hasn't interacted recently. The design flaw was coupling event delivery to immediate wake success.

Two layers contributed:
1. The timer layer was too eager to discard already-enqueued events when heartbeat failed
2. The heartbeat layer's per-agent config gates treated cron-sourced wakes the same as regular heartbeats, even though cron manages its own retry and scheduling policy

---

## Root Cause

**Layer 1 — Timer layer**: The system event was enqueued before the heartbeat attempt (line ~1990). When heartbeat failed, the cleanup code removed the event — discarding work already done.

**Layer 2 — Heartbeat layer**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` checked `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` unconditionally. Agents without explicit heartbeat config (e.g., `{id: "main"}` without `heartbeat: {every: ...}`) would always return `skipped/disabled` — even when the wake was triggered by cron. Additionally, the scheduler's `run()` returned `skipped/disabled` when the target agent was not in `state.agents` (agents without explicit heartbeat config are not tracked by the scheduler).

Together these two layers caused cron→main system event deliveries to fail silently on every attempt.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat returns skipped/error; request background heartbeat instead of removing event. Bypass per-agent heartbeat config gates for cron-sourced wakes. Preserve skipped/error status so one-shot retry behavior and job visibility are maintained.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 / Node.js v24.1.0 / OpenClaw `fix/issue-101537-cron-main-systemevent-skip-disabled`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run` targeted test commands as shown below, each exercising real production functions at L2 level (real `runHeartbeatOnce`, real system event queue, real CronJob objects).

**After-fix evidence**:

L2+ evidence (real function calls, real objects, real system event queue):
```
$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts -t "does not return disabled for cron"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)

$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts -t "routes cron targeted wakes"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 25 skipped (26)

$ npx vitest run src/cron/service.main-job-passes-heartbeat-target-last.test.ts -t "does not skip with"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 3 skipped (4)

$ node --import tsx -e 'import { isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent } from "./src/infra/heartbeat-summary.js"; console.log(isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent({agents:{list:[{id:"worker", heartbeat:{every:"5m"}}, {id:"main"}]}}, "main"));'
false  ← gate rejects main; both fix layers now bypass this for cron

$ npx tsx evidence/pr-101668/run-evidence.mjs
=== L2 Evidence ===
1. System event enqueued, events in queue before: 1
2. applyJobResult called with status="skipped", error="disabled"
   shouldDelete: false (delete only on "ok")
   job.state.lastStatus: skipped, lastError: disabled
   Job in store: YES
3. Events in queue after: 1 (preserved)
```

Full regression suites:
```
$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  44 passed (44)

$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  26 passed (26)

$ npx vitest run src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  15 passed (15)

$ npx vitest run src/cron/service.main-job-passes-heartbeat-target-last.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  4 passed (4)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Cron-sourced `runHeartbeatOnce` no longer returns `disabled` for agents without explicit heartbeat config; heartbeat scheduler routes cron-targeted wakes directly to `runOnce()`; system events are preserved through disabled-heartbeat scenarios; the job retains skipped status; background heartbeat is requested for deferred delivery.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway + cron daemon integration is not tested here. The fix is exercised through unit tests with real production functions (Vitest test framework) for the heartbeat runner, and injected dependencies for the cron timer. The complete multi-hop delivery path (heartbeat gate bypass → queue preservation → deferred delivery) is covered by the combined test suites.

---

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

Test coverage:
- ✓ keeps system event queued when disabled-heartbeat one-shot cannot wake
- ✓ disables one-shot when disabled-heartbeat retry is exhausted
- ✓ does not return disabled for cron source when agent has no explicit heartbeat config
- ✓ routes cron targeted wakes to agents without explicit heartbeat config in scheduler
- ✓ cron main job does not skip with 'disabled' when agent has no heartbeat config

### CI

CI has a pre-existing failure in `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` unrelated to this change. All 71 other CI checks pass.

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation

**Merge risk**: Low. The behavioral changes are scoped to:
1. The heartbeat-skip/error path in `executeMainSessionCronJob()` — non-ok heartbeats for cron jobs no longer discard the enqueued event
2. Cron-sourced `runHeartbeatOnce` calls — bypass per-agent config gates, preserving the global disable gate
3. Cron-targeted scheduler wakes — agents not in the scheduler's state are run directly instead of returning disabled

Global gate `areHeartbeatsEnabled()` is preserved for all sources. No new deps, no config or API changes. Rollback is a revert of this branch's commits.

**ClawSweeper P1 addressed**:
1. ✅ "Keep disabled cron wakes visible" — returning non-ok status keeps the job in the store with skipped/error state
2. ✅ "For deleteAfterRun one-shots, returning ok removes job immediately" — now returns "skipped", preserving retry behavior
3. ✅ "Add real behavior proof" — L2 evidence with real function calls showing event preservation, heartbeat gate bypass, and scheduler routing for cron sources
4. ✅ "Fix stale per-run queue and disabled heartbeat gate behavior" — by bypassing `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` for cron sources, plus direct `runOnce()` routing in the scheduler

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

## AI-assisted

This PR was created with AI assistance for code understanding, root cause analysis, test restructuring, and PR body generation. Human review was applied to all AI-generated code and tests.
