target.title: fix(session-memory): forward hook config model to LLM slug generator
target.body:
## Summary

When `llmSlug` is enabled with a `model` override in the session-memory hook config, that model was silently ignored — slug generation always resolved the agent's default model via `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`. This PR forwards the hook-level model override into the slug generator, letting `runEmbeddedAgent`'s built-in model-resolution chain handle alias, provider-qualified ref, and bare-name resolution through a single source of truth.

- **Problem**: `generateSlugViaLLM` unconditionally calls `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` and passes both `provider` and `model` to `runEmbeddedAgent`. The session-memory handler never forwards `hookConfig.model`, so any hook-level model override is silently dropped.
- **Solution**: Add an optional `model` parameter to `generateSlugViaLLM`. When the hook provides a model, pass only that model (omit provider) so `runEmbeddedAgent`'s `resolveInitialEmbeddedRunModel` handles resolution. When no hook model is provided, behavior is unchanged — provider and model both come from `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`.
- **What changed**: `src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.ts` (optional `model` param + conditional provider routing), `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.ts` (forward `hookConfig.model`), `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/HOOK.md` (document `model` config key), `src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts` (+3 tests covering bare model, provider-qualified ref, default fallback), `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts` (+2 tests covering forward and omit cases)
- **What did NOT change**: Default model resolution when no hook model is configured; provider selection; error-payload rejection; timeout handling; session-memory file format; zod schema (HookConfigSchema already uses `.passthrough()`)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #89551
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The session-memory hook's `model` field is an existing passthrough key in the hook config schema (HookConfigSchema uses `.passthrough()`), but it has never been wired into the slug-generation path. Users who configure a specific model for slug generation — especially those running lightweight local models as their agent default — expect the hook to respect that override. Currently, every `/reset` or `/new` fires an LLM call using the agent's primary model, ignoring the user's explicit configuration.

Four prior PRs (#89561, #89905, #89955, #95049) attempted this fix but were closed unmerged. The primary blocker was architectural: all four duplicated model resolution logic in the slug generator instead of routing through `runEmbeddedAgent`'s built-in resolution chain. This PR avoids that pitfall by omitting `provider` when a hook model is set, allowing the runner to resolve aliases and provider-qualified refs through its canonical path.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed**: Hook-level `model` in session-memory config was ignored during LLM slug generation.
- **Real environment tested**: Fedora 38, Node v22.11.0, upstream/main @ 9a735bea03, vitest 4.1.8
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```console
$ pnpm vitest run src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

Five new/modified tests verify the full routing surface. Key parameter assertions from the test output:

| Hook config | `provider` passed to runner | `model` passed to runner | Resolution path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model: "gpt-5.5"` (bare name) | `undefined` | `"gpt-5.5"` | Runner branch 2: alias chain resolves provider from agent default |
| `model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"` (provider-qualified) | `undefined` | `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"` | Runner branch 2: `resolveModelRefFromString` extracts provider |
| (no model configured) | `"openai"` (from config) | `"gpt-5.5"` (from config) | Runner branch 1: unchanged legacy path |
| `model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"` (handler-level) | (not set — default) | (not set — default) | `generateSlugViaLLM` called with `model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"` |
| (model omitted in hook) | (not set — default) | (not set — default) | `generateSlugViaLLM` called without `model` key |

Full test run output:

```console
$ pnpm vitest run src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts > passes hook-level bare model name without
   a provider so the runner resolves both through its alias chain 2ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts > passes hook-level provider-qualified ref
   without a separate provider, letting the runner extract it 1ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts > uses the agent default model when no hook
   model override is provided 3ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts > forwards hook config model
   override to the slug generator 14ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts > does not forward model when
   hook config omits it 10ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
   Duration  4.16s
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. When `hookConfig.model` is a bare model name, the slug generator omits `provider` and passes only the model string — the runner's `resolveInitialEmbeddedRunModel` resolves the provider via its alias chain.
  2. When `hookConfig.model` is a provider-qualified ref (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`), the runner correctly extracts the provider via `resolveModelRefFromString`.
  3. When `hookConfig.model` is absent, behavior is identical to before — `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` supplies both `provider` and `model`.
  4. The session-memory handler correctly forwards `hookConfig.model` (when a string) and omits it otherwise.
  5. All 35 pre-existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression.

**Runtime evidence (real provider, `npx tsx` against live DeepSeek backend)**:

```console
=== Test 1: Agent default (no hook model) ===
  hookModel: (not set)
[llm-slug-generator] Failed to generate slug:
  ProviderAuthError: No API key found for provider "deepseek"

=== Test 2: Hook model override (gpt-4o) ===
  hookModel: gpt-4o
[llm-slug-generator] Failed to generate slug:
  FailoverError: Unknown model: deepseek/gpt-4o

=== Test 3: Hook model override (anthropic/claude-sonnet) ===
  hookModel: anthropic/claude-sonnet
[llm-slug-generator] Failed to generate slug:
  FailoverError: Unknown model: anthropic/claude-sonnet
```

**Parameter forwarding matrix (inferred from runner-framework model strings)**:

| Hook config | `provider` passed to runner | `model` passed to runner | Runner resolves as | Proof source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (not set) | `"deepseek"` (from config) | `"deepseek-chat"` (from config) | `deepseek/deepseek-chat` | Test 1: auth error confirms deepseek provider used |
| `model: "gpt-4o"` | `undefined` | `"gpt-4o"` | `deepseek/gpt-4o` | Test 2: model is `gpt-4o` NOT agent default `deepseek-chat` |
| `model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet"` | `undefined` | `"anthropic/claude-sonnet"` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet` | Test 3: full ref forwarded, runner extracts provider |

**Key observation from Test 2**: The runner resolved `deepseek/gpt-4o` — it used the agent's default provider (`deepseek`) with the hook-level model (`gpt-4o`). This confirms:
1. The hook model override IS being forwarded to the runner (not dropped).
2. The provider is correctly omitted by our code, leaving the runner's branch 2 (`explicitModel` only path) to resolve the provider from agent defaults.
3. Without our fix, Test 2 would have used `deepseek-chat` (agent default model), identical to Test 1.

- **What was not tested**:
  - Successful LLM slug generation (requires agent auth store configuration, which is outside scope of this change).
  - Live gateway `/reset` path: blocked by `acpx` + `diffs` build dependencies on upstream/main HEAD (pnpm v9 vs v11 lockfile incompatibility), unrelated to this change.

## Root Cause

The slug generator (`llm-slug-generator.ts:95-98`) unconditionally resolves both `provider` and `model` from `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`, and the session-memory handler (`handler.ts:236`) calls it without forwarding `hookConfig.model`. The hook config schema already supports a `model` passthrough key via `HookConfigSchema.passthrough()`, but no code consumed it for slug generation.

**Provenance**: `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` replaced hardcoded defaults in commit `588ad7fb381a` (@bigwest60), establishing the current behavior where the agent's primary model always wins. The hook-level model override was never wired in.

**Confidence**: `clear` — source inspection confirms a single call site with a single missing parameter.

## Regression Test Plan

The five new tests cover the full routing surface: bare model names, provider-qualified refs, default fallback, handler forwarding, and handler omission. All 35 pre-existing tests in both test files continue to pass. The fix is limited to the slug-generation path and does not alter any other hook or model-resolution behavior.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users who set `hooks.internal.entries["session-memory"].model` will now see that model used for LLM slug generation instead of the agent's primary model. Users who do not configure a `model` key see no change.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios**: Bare model name param forwarding, provider-qualified ref forwarding, default fallback, handler-level model extraction from passthrough config, handler omission case
- **Edge cases checked**: Empty/undefined hookConfig, missing `model` key, non-string `model` value (type-guarded), provider resolution when provider is omitted
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway `/reset` with a real model provider (blocked by upstream acpx build issue)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only activates when `model` is explicitly set in hook config
- [x] Config/env changes? No — `model` is an existing passthrough key, now consumed
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. This is the narrowest correct fix: forward the hook model through `runEmbeddedAgent`'s existing resolution chain instead of duplicating model resolution in the slug generator. Prior PRs (#89561, #89905, #89955, #95049) all duplicated alias/ref resolution, creating routing drift risk.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The `resolveInitialEmbeddedRunModel` function already handles all model resolution cases (explicit provider+model, model-only with alias resolution, default fallback). No refactoring is needed to support this use case.
- **Alternative considered**: Duplicating `buildModelAliasIndex` + `resolveModelRefFromString` in the slug generator (prior PR approach) — rejected because it creates a second source of truth for model resolution, causing routing drift if the runner contract changes.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Activating `hooks.internal.entries.session-memory.model` changes provider/model routing for users who already have this passthrough key in their config. Users who set `model` expecting no behavioral change will now see it take effect.

**Mitigation**: The key was previously silently ignored, so any user who set it intended it to work. Documentation is updated in HOOK.md to describe accepted values and fallback behavior.

Related to #61213
  
## What Problem This Solves

The Web Control UI displays raw machine-generated identifiers in session
labels, making it impossible for operators to quickly identify sessions:

- Activity log shows `agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_67075ec667cac0a7feae2c5094fd27b2`
instead of a readable label like `Feishu · ou_67075ec66…`
- Exec approval dialogs show the same raw session keys

CHANNEL_LABELS, so even the fallback display was unhelpful

The proposed fix priority from #61213: binding.comment → agent.name →
technical identifier. This PR handles the UI-side display improvements.
Server-side binding.comment propagation will be a follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `CHANNEL_LABELS` only had 9 Western platforms; 18 channel labels added
- `activity.ts` and `exec-approval.ts` rendered `sessionKey` raw without any
display resolution — they now use `parseSessionKey()` for friendly fallback
- Long machine-generated identifiers (>20 chars, like `ou_` open_ids and
UUIDs) now truncate to keep the UI compact, with the full key preserved
via the `title` attribute on hover

target.title: feat(plugins): add Control UI entry points
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Plugins can expose gateway-authenticated HTTP routes, but there was no generic way for a plugin to register a first-class Control UI navigation entry.
- What changed: Added generic Plugin UI Entry Points across the plugin registry, gateway protocol, launch-token plumbing, and Control UI navigation/rendering.
- Security follow-up: Plugin UI entry registration, launch/session auth, and iframe bridge proxying now validate canonical decoded plugin roots, so encoded dot-segment paths cannot let one plugin UI session authorize sibling plugin routes.
- Scope boundary: This PR does not add the Session Search plugin or any plugin-specific UI. The proof plugin lives separately on [`Ittiz/openclaw@forge/session-search-plugin`](https://github.com/Ittiz/openclaw/tree/forge/session-search-plugin).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins can expose gateway-authenticated HTTP routes, but before this PR they had no generic, first-class way to place a Control UI navigation entry that launches a plugin-owned UI through the gateway authorization boundary. This PR adds that contract while keeping plugin entry paths and iframe bridge requests confined to the owning plugin root.

## Working Example Plugin

The working example is the Session Search plugin on the plugin-only proof branch:

- Branch: [`Ittiz/openclaw@forge/session-search-plugin`](https://github.com/Ittiz/openclaw/tree/forge/session-search-plugin)
- README: [`README.md`](https://github.com/Ittiz/openclaw/blob/forge/session-search-plugin/README.md)
- Entry point registration: [`index.ts`](https://github.com/Ittiz/openclaw/blob/forge/session-search-plugin/index.ts)
- Manifest: [`openclaw.plugin.json`](https://github.com/Ittiz/openclaw/blob/forge/session-search-plugin/openclaw.plugin.json)

That branch intentionally contains only plugin files, not the OpenClaw source tree.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Current head tested: `b8e35876a18a36390c867080e475d53f26fb4e15`.
- Behavior addressed: Plugin UI entry points can be listed/launched/rendered; sandboxed opaque-origin iframes receive the MessagePort bridge; decoded/canonicalized plugin paths remain confined to the owning plugin root; new entry-point response schemas are exported through the public protocol barrel.
- Real environment tested: rebuilt exact-head local Linux checkout, throwaway loopback gateway on `127.0.0.1:19888`, temporary plugin loaded through `plugins.load.paths`, Control UI driven in a real headless Chromium browser, plus direct HTTP route checks.

Commands run after the current fix:

Specific regression locked in:

- `ui/src/ui/navigation.browser.test.ts` verifies sandboxed in-app plugin requests are proxied only for plugin-owned paths and stale iframe bridge ports cannot service current-frame requests.
- `src/gateway/server.plugin-http-auth.test.ts` rejects Plugin UI Entry Point sessions when decoded path candidates leave the plugin root.

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes. Plugins can expose Control UI entry points.
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? Yes. Entry-point launch uses short-lived Plugin UI launch/session tokens.

- Mitigation: Entry-point paths are constrained to canonical plugin-owned roots; launch/session auth and iframe proxying reject decoded sibling escapes; direct unauthenticated plugin route access remains blocked.

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config/env changes? No.
- Migration needed? No.

Exclude it from error logging. Also downgrade aborted/restart stop reasons to console.warn since those are intentional user/system cancellations, not failures. Fixes #101678 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where successful agent run completions (`stopReason=stop`) were logged at `console.error` severity. Operators monitoring error logs would see false alarms on every normal run completion. ## Why This Change Was Made `stopReason=stop` is a normal model completion, equivalent to `end_turn` which was already silently excluded. The condition only excluded `end_turn`, so `stop` fell through to `console.error`. The fix excludes `stop` from error logging entirely, and also downgrades `aborted`/`restart` stop reasons from `console.error` to `console.warn` since those are intentional user/system cancellations, not failures. ## User Impact Operators and developers no longer see spurious error-level log entries for successful agent runs. Actual failures (`timeout`, `error`) still log at error level. Intentional cancellations log at warn level. ## Evidence Script simulating `emitLifecycleEnd` with each stop reason, before and after the fix:

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback now rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait:

- The direct-dispatcher and synthesized-voice paths keep their optimistic queued gating and capture the pre-send final-outcome counts.
- When a captioned final (or its synthesized-voice sibling) is admitted through the raw dispatcher, a post-settlement task is registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` — the same seam the transcript mirror uses. It runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path.
- That task compares the post-settlement final-outcome counts against the pre-send snapshot; if the captioned voice failed or cancelled asynchronously it re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final, so suppressed content is never silently dropped. On success it does nothing, so there is no duplicate text.

This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix: plugin tests fail on hosts with a usable /tmp/openclaw or a source checkout
target.body:
Closes #101876

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where three plugin test cases fail on any POSIX host with a normal `/tmp/openclaw` state or a source checkout (developer laptops, warm CI boxes), blocking green local runs of the plugins shard:

- `src/plugins/git-install.test.ts > falls back to OS temp when target workspace creation fails`
- `src/plugins/manifest-model-id-normalization.test.ts > reuses manifest metadata while file fingerprints are unchanged`
- `src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts > reloads when gateway binding would otherwise reuse a default-mode active registry`

## Why This Change Was Made

The three failures have three distinct causes — recent prod changes landed with stale test expectations; this PR updates only the tests to the current prod contracts (no prod behavior changes):

1. **git-install**: #101246 made `withTempDir` root fallback staging at `resolvePreferredOpenClawTmpDir()` (prefers `/tmp/openclaw`, degrades to a uid-scoped `os.tmpdir()` path when unsafe), but the test still asserted bare `os.tmpdir()`. The test now recomputes the resolver output, so the assertion holds in every resolver state.
2. **manifest scan**: 26c0285812b added the source-checkout manifest metadata fallback, so `listOpenClawPluginManifestMetadata` legitimately lists all repo `extensions/` manifests when tests run from a checkout (140 records, not 1). The test now pins exactly one record for the plugin under test and keeps the fingerprint-reuse assertion (manifest file read exactly once across two scans).
3. **tools.optional**: #100990 requires initialized registry collections (`registryHasPluginHostCleanupWork` no longer optional-chains), and updated most test registries but missed this hand-rolled `{plugins, tools, diagnostics} as never` fake, which crashes when retired. The test now uses `createEmptyPluginRegistry()`, which also drops the `as never` cast.

Note: the issue attributes all three failures to the temp-root mechanism; investigation showed only the git-install test is temp-root-coupled. The other two are stale expectations from the July 6–7 prod changes above.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Developers and CI hosts get deterministic plugin-shard test results regardless of `/tmp/openclaw` state (present, absent, or unsafe) and regardless of running from a source checkout.

## Evidence

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/git-install.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-model-id-normalization.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts` (macOS, worktree of e7365d41d35):

- Before: `Tests 3 failed | 95 passed (98)` — reproducing the issue exactly.
- After, with `/tmp/openclaw` present and safe: `Tests 98 passed (98)`.
- After, with `/tmp/openclaw` absent (resolver creates it): `Tests 98 passed (98)`.
- After, with `/tmp/openclaw` unsafe (symlink → uid-scoped `os.tmpdir()` fallback): `git-install.test.ts 23 passed (23)` (the only resolver-coupled file).
- Full plugins shard (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins`): pass (see CI for the hosted run).

`oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on the three changed files.

target.title: fix(acp): pass resolved session entry to transcript writer; surface bail errors
target.body:
## Summary

Spawn-child ACP sessions advertise a `sessionFile` path on disk, but no openclaw-side transcript was ever written there — the existing writer at `dispatch-acp.ts:517-518` was bailing silently because the disk re-load couldn't resolve the canonical session entry. Pass the already-resolved entry through, and replace the silent `console.warn` with a structured logger so future bails are visible. Closes catalog #22.

## Bug detail

Each entry in `~/.openclaw/agents/copilot/sessions/sessions.json` advertises a `sessionFile` path. For DM-driven ACP sessions (gateway-agent-method path), the file IS written. For **spawn-child** ACP sessions (Telegram supergroup-spawned, etc., dispatched via the auto-reply pipeline), the advertised file was NEVER written. openclaw-side history of those sessions was silently absent.

## How to reproduce

Live repro before fix (after a Telegram supergroup spawn-child session completes):

\`\`\`bash
docker compose exec codeclaw-openclaw bash -c '
  jq -r ".[] | select(.spawnedBy != null) | .sessionFile" /home/codeclaw/.openclaw/agents/copilot/sessions/sessions.json \
    | while read f; do
        if [ -e "$f" ]; then echo "EXISTS: $f"; else echo "MISSING: $f"; fi
      done'
# Before: every spawn-child session shows MISSING
# After:  every spawn-child session shows EXISTS
\`\`\`

Unit-level:

\`\`\`bash
git checkout 9e3e663ba1           # red-test cherry-pick
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.spawn-child-transcript.test.ts
# Before fix: 3 RED
# After fix commits 763c1e376a + dcea951cd1: all 3 GREEN
\`\`\`

## Root cause

Two writer call sites exist:

1. `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts:517-518` — calls `persistAcpDispatchTranscript` (auto-reply pipeline; spawn-child path).
2. `src/agents/agent-command.ts:580` — calls `persistAcpTurnTranscript` directly (gateway "agent" method; DM path).

Path (1) was bailing because `persistAcpDispatchTranscript` re-loaded from `loadSessionStore`, which returned no entry for the canonical session key (spawn-child entries are written via a different runtime path and weren't resolvable from the disk re-read at this point). The re-load failure threw "unknown ACP session key" inside `persistAcpDispatchTranscript`, and the throw was caught and swallowed at `dispatch-acp.ts:526-531` via `logVerbose`. Spawn-child sessions silently produced nothing.

Path (2) already had the resolved entry in scope and worked correctly.

## Fix approach

Catalog Option 1 (smallest, cleanest):

1. **Pass the resolved entry through.** `tryDispatchAcpReply` now passes the already-resolved `AcpSessionStoreEntry` (loaded via `readAcpSessionEntry` through the existing `loadDispatchAcpSessionRuntime` mock seam) into `persistAcpDispatchTranscript` as an optional `sessionStoreEntry` parameter.
2. **Skip the disk re-load when entry is supplied.** Inside `persistAcpDispatchTranscript`, when `sessionStoreEntry?.entry?.sessionId` is present, build a minimal `Record<string, SessionEntry>` from it for `persistAcpTurnTranscript`'s shape contract. Fallback to `loadSessionStore` is preserved for callers that don't supply the entry.
3. **Make bails visible.** Replaced the `console.warn` at `dispatch-acp.ts:537` with a structured `log.warn` via `createSubsystemLogger("dispatch-acp")` — matches the parallel pattern used by `agent-command.ts` and the codebase convention in `session.ts`. Future bails will surface in operator logs without verbose mode set.
4. **Narrow the type cast** in `dispatch-acp-transcript.runtime.ts` from a broad `as ReturnType<typeof loadSessionStore>` to an explicit non-null assertion `preResolved.entry!` against the narrower `Record<string, SessionEntry>`.

The parallel writer at `agent-command.ts:580` is unchanged — it already works for DM-driven flows.

## Tests

- **Red test (now GREEN):** `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.spawn-child-transcript.test.ts` — 3 cases pass.
- **Adjacent suite:** `src/auto-reply/reply/` — 1538 pass / 0 fail.

## Catalog reference

Catalog finding: #22. Investigation lives in branch `edpiva/acp-native-session-investigation` (not yet upstream) at `docs/plans/2026-05-08-acp-findings-catalog.md`.

## Verification commands

\`\`\`bash
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.spawn-child-transcript.test.ts   # 3/3 GREEN
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/                                              # 1538/0
\`\`\`

## Notes for reviewers

- The new `sessionStoreEntry` parameter on `persistAcpDispatchTranscript` is optional, so existing callers (if any) keep working without modification.
- The synthetic `{ [params.sessionKey]: preResolved.entry! }` is only there to satisfy `persistAcpTurnTranscript`'s `sessionStore` parameter shape — the actual write goes through `sessionEntry`, which is passed directly. Refactoring `persistAcpTurnTranscript` to take a single entry instead of a store is a follow-up worth doing if you'd prefer it now.
- The new module-scope `log = createSubsystemLogger("dispatch-acp")` matches the agent-command.ts pattern; this file had no pre-existing logger.

---

## Live behavior repro (deployed container)

**Container:** `codeclaw-openclaw:clean` running OpenClaw 2026.5.6 (`e9d4a0a`)
**PII note:** Telegram chat/group/topic IDs redacted to `<chat-id>` / `<topic-id>`. Path prefix `/home/codeclaw/` is the public deployment user.

### Spawn-child sessions can silently fail to write their advertised `sessionFile`

Walking the in-container sessions store and checking each advertised `sessionFile`:

```
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw bash -c 'jq -r "to_entries[] | select(.value.spawnedBy != null) | .value.sessionFile // empty" \
    /home/codeclaw/.openclaw/agents/copilot/sessions/sessions.json \
    | while read f; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then echo "EXISTS: $f"; else echo "MISSING: $f"; fi; done'

EXISTS: <store>/18a09361-…jsonl     spawnedBy: telegram:group:<chat-id>:topic:<topic-id>
EXISTS: <store>/1978341a-…jsonl     spawnedBy: telegram:group:<chat-id>:topic:<topic-id>
EXISTS: <store>/24843f10-…jsonl     spawnedBy: telegram:default:direct:<chat-id>      (DM)
EXISTS: <store>/5244dd04-…jsonl     spawnedBy: telegram:default:direct:<chat-id>      (DM)
EXISTS: <store>/b1876021-…jsonl     spawnedBy: telegram:default:direct:<chat-id>      (DM)
EXISTS: <store>/e421061f-…jsonl     spawnedBy: telegram:default:direct:<chat-id>      (DM)
MISSING: <store>/7de23a0a-…jsonl    spawnedBy: telegram:group:<chat-id>:topic:<topic-id>
```

The behavior is silent and intermittent — the catalog framing of "spawn-child sessions NEVER write" was too strong. **Refined finding:** spawn-child sessions can silently *fail* to write because the writer at `dispatch-acp.ts:517-518` re-loaded from `loadSessionStore`, which sometimes returned no entry for the canonical session key (entries written via a different runtime path were not yet readable). The thrown error was caught and swallowed at lines 526-531 via `logVerbose`, leaving operators with no signal that history had been lost for that session.

After this PR (fix `763c1e376a` + cleanup `dcea951cd1`), the resolved `AcpSessionStoreEntry` flows from the call site directly into `persistAcpDispatchTranscript`, skipping the lossy re-load. The catch path now logs visibly via the structured `dispatch-acp` subsystem logger, so future bails are observable.

target.title: feat(acp): add sessions link helper for operator diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

Add `openclaw sessions link` — a read-only diagnostic helper that prints the three-identifier triple operators currently have to walk by hand to correlate an ACP session across openclaw and copilot. Closes catalog #8.

## Bug detail

Two distinct identifiers refer to the same ACP session, and operators have had to discover the mapping by reading individual session JSON files:

- **openclaw side:** `agent:copilot:acp:<uuid>` (file basename in `~/.openclaw/workspace/state/sessions/agent%3Acopilot%3Aacp%3A<uuid>.json`)
- **copilot side:** `<acp_session_id>` (directory name in `~/.copilot/session-state/<acp_session_id>/events.jsonl`)
- **Join field:** `acp.identity.acpxSessionId` inside the openclaw session record

Live diagnosis (e.g., "what events did copilot emit for the run that's stuck in topic 315?") required walking openclaw's session files, finding the one whose binding matches the topic, reading its `acpxSessionId`, then jumping to copilot's directory under that name. There was no single command, no aggregated index, and no explicit cross-reference printed to logs.

## How to reproduce

Before fix:

\`\`\`bash
# Walk by hand to correlate one session — three commands per session
ls ~/.openclaw/workspace/state/sessions/ | grep acp
jq '.acp.identity.acpxSessionId' ~/.openclaw/workspace/state/sessions/<file>
ls ~/.copilot/session-state/<that-uuid>/
\`\`\`

After this PR:

\`\`\`bash
openclaw sessions link            # one command, full triple per session
openclaw sessions link --json     # machine-parseable
\`\`\`

## Root cause

No tooling existed; the three identifiers and their join field were undocumented (also addressed in the docs PR for catalog #7/#14/#23). Tests exist for the underlying types, but no command surfaced the join.

## Fix approach

New `openclaw sessions link` subcommand. Read-only; no mutation. Walks `~/.openclaw/workspace/state/sessions/agent%3A*%3Aacp%3A*.json`, reads `entry.acp.identity.acpxSessionId`, resolves the copilot state directory `~/.copilot/session-state/<acpxSessionId>/`, and emits a 4-column TSV (or JSON with `--json`):

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `openclaw-key` | the `agent:<agent>:acp:<uuid>` from the file basename |
| `acp-session-id` | the resolved `acpxSessionId` |
| `copilot-state-path` | the absolute path to copilot's session-state dir |
| `status` | one of `ok`, `MISSING_STATE_DIR`, `MISSING_ACP_ID` |

Naming: `sessions link` subcommand follows the established `sessions cleanup` / `sessions export-trajectory` pattern (verb-noun subcommand, not flag).

Doc cross-reference added to `docs/plugins/reference/acpx.md` with a "Session ID join model" section.

## Tests

- **New tests:** `src/commands/acp-sessions-link.test.ts` — 11 cases:
  - Happy path: full triple emitted
  - `MISSING_STATE_DIR`: `acpxSessionId` present but copilot state dir missing
  - `MISSING_ACP_ID`: no `acpxSessionId` at all
  - Empty store, non-ACP entries filtered, missing store file, JSON output, no-sessions message, etc.
- **Adjacent:** `sessions.test.ts` 13/0; `agent.acp.test.ts` 7/0

## Catalog reference

Catalog finding: #8. Investigation lives in branch `edpiva/acp-native-session-investigation` (not yet upstream) at `docs/plans/2026-05-08-acp-findings-catalog.md`.

## Verification commands

\`\`\`bash
pnpm test src/commands/acp-sessions-link.test.ts                # 11/11 GREEN
pnpm test src/commands/sessions.test.ts src/commands/agent.acp.test.ts   # 20/20 GREEN
\`\`\`

## Notes for reviewers

- Output format: TSV with a header row and uppercase status sentinels (`ok`, `MISSING_STATE_DIR`, `MISSING_ACP_ID`). Machine-parseable AND human-readable. `--json` flag for tooling integrations.
- Doc location: the Task spec referenced `docs/extensions/acpx.md`, but the actual file lives at `docs/plugins/reference/acpx.md` (verified on `origin/main`). Used the real path.
- Scope: read-only diagnostic. No session mutation. Flags are minimal: `--store` (override store path), `--agent` (filter to one agent), `--json` (output format).

---

## Live behavior repro (deployed container)

**Container:** `codeclaw-openclaw:clean` running OpenClaw 2026.5.6 (`e9d4a0a`)
**PII note:** UUIDs are random; no PII to redact in this slice.

### Today: three commands per session to walk the ACP join model

There is no single command that prints `openclaw key → acp_session_id → copilot state path`. Operators currently chain three lookups manually:

```
# 1. List ACP session records on disk
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw ls ~/.openclaw/workspace/state/sessions/ | grep acp
agent%3Acopilot%3Aacp%3A1f854fa2-…%3Aoneshot%3A7c6105aa-….json
agent%3Acopilot%3Aacp%3A86b7b5af-….json
…

# 2. Pull the join field from one record
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw jq '.acp.identity.acpxSessionId' \
    ~/.openclaw/workspace/state/sessions/agent%3Acopilot%3Aacp%3A1f854fa2-….json
"<acp-session-id-uuid>"

# 3. Find copilot's session-state directory under that uuid
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw ls ~/.copilot/session-state/<acp-session-id-uuid>/
events.jsonl  …
```

After this PR, one read-only command surfaces the full triple plus a status sentinel for missing state dirs:

```
$ openclaw sessions link
openclaw-key                                    acp-session-id      copilot-state-path                          status
agent:copilot:acp:1f854fa2-…:oneshot:7c6105aa-…  <uuid-1>           /home/codeclaw/.copilot/session-state/<…>   ok
agent:copilot:acp:86b7b5af-…                     <uuid-2>           /home/codeclaw/.copilot/session-state/<…>   MISSING_STATE_DIR
agent:copilot:acp:d6fb7506-…                     —                  —                                            MISSING_ACP_ID
```

Adds `--json` for tooling and a doc cross-reference at `docs/plugins/reference/acpx.md` so the join model is also discoverable from prose.

target.title: fix(acp): capture and persist usage_update tokens for ACP sessions
target.body:
## Summary

Plumb token usage from ACP `usage_update` events into the openclaw session record so `totalTokens` is no longer permanently `null` for ACP sessions. Closes catalog #21.

## Bug detail

Every ACP session in the listing reported `totalTokens: null`, `totalTokensFresh: false`, regardless of how many turns it had run. The acpx session record carried `cumulative_token_usage: {}` and `request_token_usage: {}` (empty), confirming token usage was never being persisted from the copilot ACP runtime into the openclaw session entry. Token-cost tracking and budget guards were inoperative for any ACP session.

## How to reproduce

Live repro before fix:

\`\`\`bash
docker compose exec codeclaw-openclaw openclaw sessions --all-agents --json \
  | jq '.sessions[] | select(.key | contains("acp:")) | {key, totalTokens, totalTokensFresh}'
# Before: all ACP sessions show "totalTokens": null, "totalTokensFresh": false
# After: ACP sessions that completed a turn show numeric totalTokens
\`\`\`

Unit-level repro:

\`\`\`bash
git checkout 5e083f0510            # red-test cherry-pick
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.usage-update-tokens.test.ts
# Before fix: 2 RED (callback never fires; persistence bucket stays unset)
# After fix commit d292fa7199: all 3 GREEN
\`\`\`

## Root cause

`src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts:462-474` consumed `usage_update` events for **display only** (`emitSystemStatus(event.text, ...)`). Numeric `event.used` / `event.size` were extracted just for repeat-suppression hashing — never persisted. There was no callback or write path from the projector back to the session record. `resolveSessionTotalTokens` (`src/config/sessions/types.ts:506-514`) reads `entry?.totalTokens` which therefore stayed `null`.

## Fix approach

Catalog Option 1 — write entry-level `totalTokens` via the existing `persistSessionUsageUpdate` helper. No new schema fields:

1. Added optional `onTokenUsage?: (usage: AcpTokenUsage) => void | Promise<void>` parameter to `createAcpReplyProjector`. Existing callers compile unchanged.
2. The projector fires `onTokenUsage({ used, size, total: used })` BEFORE the display dedupe/visibility gate, so persistence always receives the latest values regardless of repeat-suppression. Guarded by `event.tag === "usage_update" && typeof event.used === "number" && typeof event.size === "number"` — text-only `usage_update` events do not trigger the callback.
3. `dispatch-acp.ts` wires the callback to call `persistSessionUsageUpdate({ usage: { input: usage.used, output: 0 }, usageIsContextSnapshot: true, contextTokensUsed: usage.size })`. Because `usageIsContextSnapshot: true`, `deriveSessionTotalTokens` writes the captured value to `entry.totalTokens` — the exact field `resolveSessionTotalTokens` already reads.
4. ACP `usage_update` events do not separate input from output, so all tokens are lumped into `input` (with `output: 0`). The `usageIsContextSnapshot` semantics treat this as a context snapshot rather than incremental usage.

## Tests

- **Red test (now GREEN):** `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.usage-update-tokens.test.ts` — 3 cases: 2 formerly-red flip GREEN, 1 GREEN control stays GREEN.
- **Adjacent suite:** `src/auto-reply/reply/` — 1538 pass / 0 fail / 115 files. No regressions.
- **Cleanup commit (`1ba8b529a5`):** removed dead pre-fix shim from the test file and added a one-line WHY comment at the projector's `onTokenUsage` call site.

## Catalog reference

Catalog finding: #21. Investigation lives in branch `edpiva/acp-native-session-investigation` (not yet upstream) at `docs/plans/2026-05-08-acp-findings-catalog.md`.

## Verification commands

\`\`\`bash
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.usage-update-tokens.test.ts   # 3/3 GREEN
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/                                            # 1538/0
\`\`\`

## Notes for reviewers

- ACP doesn't separate input/output token counts, so the persisted value lumps everything into `input` with `output: 0`. This matches what the catalog finding flagged as the trade-off for option 1; if you'd prefer extending `SessionAcpMeta` with explicit fields instead, I can switch (option 2 in the catalog).
- The optional callback parameter is intentionally additive — no breaking change to existing projector callers.
- `resolveSessionTotalTokens` was reached without modification: option 1 writes `entry.totalTokens` and the existing reader handles it.

---

## Live behavior repro (deployed container)

**Container:** `codeclaw-openclaw:clean` running OpenClaw 2026.5.6 (`e9d4a0a`)

### `totalTokens` permanently `null` for every ACP session

```
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw openclaw sessions --all-agents --json \
    | jq -c '.sessions[] | select(.key | startswith("agent:copilot:acp:")) | {key, totalTokens, totalTokensFresh}'

{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:86b7b5af-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:d6fb7506-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:f5ab8dba-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:1f854fa2-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:930316f7-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:63867cf7-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
{"key":"agent:copilot:acp:8fb42bab-…","totalTokens":null,"totalTokensFresh":false}
```

7/7 ACP sessions report `null` even after multiple turns. The acpx record carries `cumulative_token_usage: {}` and `request_token_usage: {}` (empty) — token usage was never plumbed from the copilot ACP runtime into the openclaw entry. Token-cost tracking and budget guards were inoperative for any ACP session.

After this PR (fix commit `d292fa7199`), the projector fires `onTokenUsage` whenever a `usage_update` event lands with numeric `used`/`size`, which triggers `persistSessionUsageUpdate` → `entry.totalTokens` is populated and `resolveSessionTotalTokens` returns the correct value.

target.body:
## Summary

Adds the complete non-mutating **Claws** validation slice in one PR:

- `openclaw.claw.v1` manifest schema, parser, diagnostics, and fixtures.
- Local `openclaw claws inspect` for validation and summary.
- Local feed support for `claw` entries plus `openclaw claws feed inspect`.
- Artifact/provenance preview for package-like entries using existing selector parsers.
- Local and feed `apply --dry-run --json` lifecycle plans.
- Real CLI E2E coverage for inspect, feed inspect, dry-run apply, feed dry-run apply, and fail-closed non-dry-run apply.

This PR intentionally does **not** add mutating apply, artifact installation, workspace writes, automation enablement, provenance persistence, ClawHub publishing/search, or Gateway state changes.

## Command surface

target.title: feat(sessions): add local timezone prefix to archive filenames
target.body:
Session archive filenames now include an optional local-date prefix when
a timezone is configured, keeping the UTC timestamp for compatibility.

Format: `<file>.jsonl.<reason>.<local-date>_<utc-timestamp>`
Example: `abc.jsonl.reset.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z`

When no timezone is configured, falls back to current UTC-only behavior.

Key changes:
- `artifacts.ts`: `ARCHIVE_TIMESTAMP_RE` accepts optional `YYYY-MM-DD_` prefix
- `formatSessionArchiveTimestamp` accepts optional `timeZone` parameter
- `restoreSessionArchiveTimestamp` strips prefix before UTC parsing
- Thread `timeZone` through archive chain (`archiveFileOnDisk` → `archiveSessionTranscripts*`)
- Extract `userTimezone` from `cfg` in reset (`session-reset-service`) and delete (`sessions.ts`) paths
- Manual compact, maintenance ops, and doctor commands keep UTC behavior

Fixes #96611

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in non-UTC timezones (e.g., Asia/Shanghai UTC+8) could not reliably find archived session files by local date. Session archive filenames used UTC timestamps, causing sessions after 16:00 UTC to be filed under the previous date — for a UTC+8 user, any session between 00:00–07:59 local time was mislabeled as the previous UTC date. Roughly half of a typical week's archived sessions showed the wrong date, making local-date-based session discovery unreliable.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Option B was chosen**: add a local-date prefix (`YYYY-MM-DD_`) while keeping the UTC timestamp suffix, rather than replacing the UTC timestamp entirely. This preserves backward compatibility — old-format filenames without the prefix continue to be recognized by the archive parser, cleanup code, and usage accounting. The prefix is purely decorative for discovery purposes; the canonical UTC timestamp remains machine-parseable. Non-user-facing paths (maintenance operations, doctor commands, manual compact) do not receive a timezone and gracefully fall back to UTC, minimizing risk.

## User Impact

Users with `agents.defaults.userTimezone` configured (e.g., `"Asia/Shanghai"`) will now see archive filenames prefixed with their local date, making it easy to find archived sessions by local date when browsing the filesystem. 
Users without a timezone configured see no change — behavior is identical to before.

## Evidence
### 1. Configured timezone produces local-date prefix

`agents.defaults.userTimezone: "Asia/Shanghai"`, UTC timestamp `2026-06-24T17:00:00.000Z`:

| Function | Output |
|----------|--------|
| `formatSessionArchiveTimestamp(ms, "Asia/Shanghai")` | `2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` |
| Full archive filename | `abc.jsonl.reset.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` |

The local date prefix `2026-06-25` correctly reflects Beijing time for a session at 01:00 local.

### 2. No timezone config keeps UTC-only behavior

`userTimezone` unset or `undefined`:

| Function | Output |
|----------|--------|
| `formatSessionArchiveTimestamp(ms)` | `2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` |
| `formatSessionArchiveTimestamp(ms, undefined)` | `2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` |

No local-date prefix — unchanged from current behavior.

### 3. Old-format backward compatibility

Old UTC-only filenames without the prefix are still correctly handled:

| Function | Input | Result |
|----------|-------|--------|
| `isSessionArchiveArtifactName` | `abc.jsonl.reset.2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` | `true` |
| `parseSessionArchiveTimestamp` | same, reason `"reset"` | `1741870800000` (correct) |
| `parseUsageCountedSessionIdFromFileName` | same | `"abc"` |
| `isUsageCountedSessionTranscriptFileName` | same | `true` |

### 4. New-format parsing

Timezone-prefixed filenames are correctly parsed:

| Function | Input | Result |
|----------|-------|--------|
| `isSessionArchiveArtifactName` | `abc.jsonl.reset.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` | `true` |
| `parseSessionArchiveTimestamp` | same, reason `"reset"` | `1741870800000` (correct) |
| `parseSessionArchiveTimestamp` | same, reason `"deleted"` | `null` (correct — wrong reason) |
| `parseUsageCountedSessionIdFromFileName` | same | `"abc"` |
| `isUsageCountedSessionTranscriptFileName` | same | `true` |

### 5. Delete and bak archives also work

| Reason | Filename | Classified | Parsed |
|--------|----------|-----------|--------|
| `deleted` | `def.jsonl.deleted.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` | `true` | `1741870800000` |
| `bak` | `ghi.jsonl.bak.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-00.000Z` | `true` | `1741870800000` |

Bak archives correctly excluded from usage counting (expected — `isUsageCounted` returns `false`).

### 6. Test run

All 13 tests pass — 8 existing tests unchanged, 5 new tests covering timezone prefix behavior:

```
 ✓ classifies archived artifact file names
 ✓ classifies orphaned session store atomic-write temp files
 ✓ classifies primary transcript files
 ✓ classifies trajectory sidecar artifacts
 ✓ classifies usage-counted transcript files
 ✓ parses usage-counted session ids from file names
 ✓ parses exact compaction checkpoint transcript file names
 ✓ formats and parses archive timestamps
 ✓ falls back instead of throwing for out-of-range archive timestamps
 ✓ formats archive timestamps with timezone prefix
 ✓ parses archive timestamps with timezone prefix
 ✓ classifies archived artifact files with timezone prefix
 ✓ handles usage-counted session ids with timezone-prefixed filenames

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Timer regression (49 tests) | ✅ All passed |
| Failure-alert (7 tests) | ✅ All passed |

### Key verified behaviors

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual at-job error | `enabled` stays true, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| Manual success | `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown preserved ✅ |
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun | Job NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun | Job deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |


## Real CLI proof (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway at `885d605e56` running with `--allow-unconfigured`.

**Terminal transcript**: `openclaw cron add` → `cron show` → `cron run` (manual, triggers error) → `cron show` (job still exists, enabled=true, nextRunAtMs preserved) → `cron list` (job present) → `cron runs` (run history with error status, nextRunAtMs unchanged).

| Step | Command | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| Add job | `openclaw cron add --name proof-job --at ... --delete-after-run` | Created with `deleteAfterRun: true` |
| Manual run | `openclaw cron run <id>` | `{"ok": true, "enqueued": true}` |
| After run | `openclaw cron show <id>` | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |
| Job exists | `openclaw cron list` | Job still listed ✅ |
| Run history | `openclaw cron runs --id <id>` | `status: "error"`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |


## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| Test | Command | Before (main) | After (PR head) |
|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive `deleteAfterRun`, counter mutations, at-job disable, recurring backoff, and alert cooldown. The 12 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build Docker image from PR HEAD
docker build --target build -t openclaw-pr83933:test .

# Test 1: Timer regression tests (includes all 12 manual-run isolation tests)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

# Test 2: Failure alert tests (adapted for manual-run isolation)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts

# Test 3: Lint check
```

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. This makes manual runs safe, non-destructive operations that cannot interfere with scheduled execution. No reasonable user scenario depends on manual runs consuming one-shot jobs or driving retry/backoff state.

## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.

Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.

The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.

Unit coverage exercises the exact `applyJobResult` branch the Gateway calls internally.

## Summary
- Restacked on current `main` after #99731 merged.
- Adds review-required `doctor --fix` previews for Gateway policy findings that should not be auto-mutated:
  - `policy/gateway-non-loopback-bind`: previews setting `gateway.bind=loopback` for `gateway.bind` and `gateway.customBindHost` non-loopback findings.
  - `policy/gateway-node-command-denied`: previews appending the missing command to `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`.
- Preserves skipped repair preview `changes` in the structured repair flow so review-required guidance is visible without counting the check as repaired.
- Documents the Gateway review-required preview behavior in `docs/cli/policy.md`; no generic Doctor docs were changed.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed:
`doctor --fix` source repair flow now surfaces review-required preview guidance for Gateway bind and Gateway node-command policy findings without mutating config or counting the check as repaired.

Real environment tested:
WSL Ubuntu source checkout at PR head `c4395e6c089163d09af74dcba7a7cb7eadc6db84`, rebased on current `main`. The proof used the real Policy doctor registration plus `runDoctorHealthRepairs` against an isolated temp workspace with `plugins.entries.policy.config.workspaceRepairs=true`; no live Gateway server, provider, network call, or LLM call was started.
